name: Familiarity and Biome Preference: 40 Nature Photographs
description: Faithful replication of Mangone, Dopko & Zelenski (2021), "Deciphering landscape preferences: Investigating the roles of familiarity and biome types", Landscape and Urban Planning 214:104189, built from the authors' Qualtrics survey and its 40 photographs in their OSF materials (osf.io/4vbrj). The photos show ten biomes, four each: beach, lake, river, mountain, meadow, park, temperate forest, tropical forest, marsh and swamp. All 40 are shown one at a time in random order and each is rated on 13 seven-point items: how much people like it and would like to live next to it, how familiar, safe, public, beautiful, pleasant and relaxing it is, and five restorativeness statements (fascinating, attention drawn to many interesting things, hard to be bored, a refuge from nuisances, a place to get away). Participants then answer the six-item Nature Relatedness scale (NR-6, 1–5) and where they grew up, hometown, years in their city, age, gender and year of study. In the original study (720 students in Ottawa and Florida), beaches and lakes were strongly preferred and marshes and swamps much less, regardless of familiarity; subjective familiarity went with liking, and nature relatedness predicted liking of all biomes except beaches. Differences from the original study: (1) "How long have you lived in Ottawa?" is asked as years in the participant's current city, and "Not a student" is added to the year-of-study question; (2) the university-specific consent and debriefing text is shortened. Photographs are as distributed by the authors and are used with credit for research; they are removed if the authors or photographers object.

items.text: How much do you like this environment, for whatever reason?
How much would you like to live permanently adjacent to this environment?
How safe would you feel in this environment?
In places like this my attention is drawn to many interesting things.
In places like this it is hard to be bored.
Places like this are a refuge from nuisances.
To get away from things that usually demand my attention, I like to go to places like this.

elements.title: Ratings of the 40 nature photographs
elements.description: One row per photo (key = file stem, e.g. beach_2; the word before the number is the biome: park, river, meadow_open, swamp_florida, marsh_ottawa, temperate_forest, beach, mountain, tropical_forest, lake; 4 photos each). All 40 shown one at a time in random order. Value: 13 ratings, each 1–7: like, live, familiar, safe, public, beautiful, pleasant, relaxing (1 = Not at all … 7 = Very …), fascinating, attention, not_bored, refuge, get_away (1 = Strongly disagree … 7 = Strongly agree). The paper's positivity score = mean of all items except familiar and public.
